name: Chrony
description: Chrony is an NTP implementation that, with gpsd and a GPS receiver as its reference clock, turns the container into a stratum 1 time server for your network. It uses the GPS NMEA time and, when the receiver delivers one, its PPS signal for microsecond accuracy, with the public NTP pool as fallback.

notes.text: Plug the GPS receiver into the Proxmox host before creating the container; /dev/ttyACM0-1 and /dev/ttyUSB0-1 are passed through automatically.
Stratum 1 needs a GPS fix. Run 'chronyc sources' and wait for NMEA or PPS to be marked with '*'; tune the NMEA offset in /etc/chrony/conf.d/gps.conf if it is rejected.
PPS works only with receivers that put it on the serial DCD line (e.g. FTDI); most USB ACM receivers give NMEA-only (~1 ms) accuracy.
